posts.name: Trajector
posts.cooked:
So we played our first game with the OblivAeon heroes tonight. I was La Comodora, because I’ve been curious about her character design for a long time.

Yegads.

Every turn was total chaos, but in such a controlled way! I loved it. A few turns into the game, I had the Concordant Helm and Chronological Sweetspot in play, with Harnessed Anomaly in the trash. For the next three turns, I:

  1. Destroyed something inconsequential at the start

  2. Used La Comodora’s power to shuffle her deck and stick Harnessed Anomaly under the top card

  3. Drew a card

  4. Played a card

  5. Sweetspot tried to play all the hero decks, and oh, look, I found a Harnessed Anomaly!

Needless to say, Stuntman was very happy.

posts.name: robertmaxfreeman
posts.cooked:
La Commadora is amazing as long as you don't run out of cards. She really needs to get her wheel into play, so she can draw first, and draw 2 cards each turn. Having an ally that allows her to draw extra cards helps too. 

Akash is amazingly good, but takes a little while before her seeds start sprouting from the environment. Luckily she has 50 hit points to last her until then, and her non-seed cards are still quite good, so she's not entirely dependent on the seeds sprouting.

Writhe is my other favorite new character, especially with his Cosmic Inventor alternate. Don't worry, you'll get plenty of cards that'll retrieve his shadow cloak for you. His base power will not only load you up with cards, but protect your allies.

posts.name: Better Believe It's Andrew
posts.cooked:
Writhe wasn't clicking for me until I played Cosmic Inventor, and now I don't think I want to go back to his base power.  Cosmic Inventor just opens up so many more power options for you.

It also allows for some great combos.  Protect the target who would get hit by the Operative or the Matriarch so the team can take out one target for free per round.  Protect Scholar of the Infinite so he can use his base power without hurting himself.  Protect Akash'Thriya or Nightmist from their own self-damage...

 

I'm loving pretty much all the new heroes.  Luminary feels just perfect, where all he wants to do is throw out devices, then blow them up.  La Comodora is fantastic and may eventually slip into my favorite character slot.  Idealist is crazy good.  I used her karate robot to take down Ultimate Iron Legacy.

posts.name: Godai
posts.cooked:
We had our first game with new heroes last night. Akash’Thyria, Mainstay, and the Harpy, base versions all.

i was Mainstay, never got the Redirect Damage card, but did ok on the “destroy my own stuff for fun shenanigans” part. 

Friend played Akash, had fun seeding the Environment, and we even got a few uses out of the Tree.

Wife played Harpy, and unfortunately we had a lot of DR to get through at the start, but by the time she had 4-5 ongoing out, and the DR was dealt with, Harpy just exploded with rapid-fire damage. 

Overall, fun time, and looking forward to learning more!

posts.name: MindWanderer
posts.cooked:
I haven't played all of them yet.  My friend played Lifeline and Akash'Thriya but didn't get much mileage out of either.  I had a tough time "balancing" Harpy and ended up just going full bird mode and letting her be a machine gun--effective but off-flavor.  La Comodora worked nicely but I didn't get any incredible combos going.

Mainstay and The Idealist, on the other hand, wow.  I started the game with two Drop the Hammers in hand and drew a third early on, not what you want at the beginning.  But my other cards were generally useful and my damage output was always consistent, even when doing some ongoing or environment control.  But by the end, thanks to La Capitan, I ended up with a couple of Void Belters and Durasteel Vests in my trash.  So finally (and under a Targeting Arrow) I got to do Drop the Hammer, Drop the Hammer, Drop the Hammer, play and use Void Belter, destroy the Void Belter.  Not even close to ideal but it did work out to something like 36 damage.

Idealist did require a lot of forethought, moving fragments around to keep Strained Superego from destroying things.  That was kind of annoying.  But Karate Robot is just ridiculous.  I did need the Super Sentai power to shut off an opening-hand Monster of Id, but otherwise it was just Stabby Knives and Karate chops all day.  So much damage, and it's consistent damage, too, not giant nova rounds like so many other heroes.
